mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 6.5% in a single month, it triggers a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate tighter labor markets and reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: UNRATE does not cross the 6.5% threshold in any month, or 5-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in both demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) indices over a month predicts positive 60-day S&P 500 returns as excess demand drives equity valuations higher.
failure_condition: Neither GDPC1 nor INDPRO shows sustained growth over the month, or 60-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a 'late-cycle expansion' regime, a decline in the federal funds rate strengthens the positive 20-day return signal for the S&P 500 by reducing discount rates on future cash flows.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods, FEDFUNDS decline does not lead to significantly higher 20-day returns (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the CPIAUCSL index above 262.5 triggers negative 5-day S&P 500 returns as investors anticipate inflationary pressures eroding corporate profit margins.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL does not cross the 262.5 threshold in any month, or 5-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly PAYEMS (unemployment) falls below 140,000, it predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as investors anticipate job market improvement and consumer spending recovery.
failure_condition: PAYEMS does not fall below 140,000 in any month, or 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An INDPRO index crossing above 106.5 triggers positive 60-day S&P 500 returns as investors anticipate supply-demand balance restoration.
failure_condition: INDPRO does not cross the 106.5 threshold in any month, or 60-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in demand (GDPC1) alongside a decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals contractionary policy easing, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as discount rates on equities are reduced.
failure_condition: The combination of GDPC1 rising and FEDFUNDS falling does not occur in any month, or 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
